snippet.title: NASA’s $1.5 Billion Telescope Was Useless
snippet.description:
In 1990, NASA launched the $1.5 billion Hubble Space Telescope… and every photo came back blurry. Its giant mirror had been polished perfectly, to the wrong shape. The edge was off by about 1/50 of a human hair, because a test tool at the factory was set up wrong.

The mirror couldn’t be swapped in space. So in December 1993, astronauts on Space Shuttle Endeavour caught Hubble with the robotic arm and, over five spacewalks, installed “glasses”: COSTAR, a box of 10 small corrective mirrors.

Two years later, Hubble stared at a tiny, empty-looking patch of sky for 10 days and found over 3,000 galaxies, the famous Hubble Deep Field.

Images: NASA/ESA (M100 before the repair, Hubble Deep Field, STS-31 deployment photo).
Sources: Astronomy Magazine, ESA/Hubble, NASASpaceflight.com

snippet.description:
